terms.comment: Lewis & Short: of the body only post-Augustan (Pliny; Celsus in Morgan–Owens); in Cicero sectiō is the auction of confiscated goods.
Cicero uses it figuratively of a violent remedy (Att. 4.3.3, Lewis & Short).
Classically operātiō is a working, labour or a religious service (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: bibitur et contrā serpentēs et ante sectiōnēs pūnctiōnēsque, nē sentiantur
phrases.english: it is drunk against snakebite, and before operations and lancings, so that they are not felt

sources: Lewis & Short: sectio · Lewis & Short: chirurgia · Lewis & Short: operatio
